Subject: SSO/SCIM cutover kickoff + access constraints

Hi Tessa / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this on. We’re targeting the week of Aug 7 for the SSO cutover; before we schedule the cutover we need to confirm a few access constraints so our security/compliance team can sign off:

- SCIM: we have a custom attribute (employeeType) that must map to Redwood role assignments. Can we get a sample mapping?
- Service accounts: our platform team requires that any long-lived API/service accounts are tagged and rotate keys via our org policy; we need an example naming convention and advice for least-privilege scopes.
- IP allowlist: we use dynamic NATs in some regions — can you confirm if Redwood supports CIDR ranges (we can provide ranges) and if there is a fallback for mobile/remote users?
- Audit logs & retention: what logs will be available to us during onboarding and after cutover (30/90/365 days)?

If useful, looping in Daniel from infra/security and procurement (cc’d). Can you send a short checklist and a runbook we can run in our staging environment first?

Best,

Emily —

Thanks, this is clear and helpful. I’ve attached a concise checklist (redwood_authz_checklist.xlsx) and our first-draft playbook (authz-playbook-v1.pdf). High-level notes:

- SCIM mapping: we can support a custom attribute mapping for employeeType. Attached scim-mapping.csv shows a recommended mapping from your LDAP/Okta attributes to Redwood roles (example row included).
- Service accounts: recommend a naming convention evervale-redwood-svc-<purpose>-<env>. We’ll provide an IAM role template and an example minimal scope for token creation. Long-lived keys: recommend short-lived tokens where possible; if you must have long-lived keys, we suggest rotation every 30 days and tagging in your CMDB.
- IP allowlist: Redwood accepts CIDR ranges. For mobile users we support OAuth device flows and region-based fallback policies; we’ll document the policy to allow IP fallback for trusted user agents during cutover.
- Audit logs: during the private deployment we can provide 365-day retention by default, with exports to your SIEM. Hosted customers get 90 days; we can align on export cadence for your environment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa and I will schedule a 45-min staging runbook session with your infra team (please propose times).
2) Ben will own procurement/contract redlines that touch SLA/retention.
3) We’ll produce a final cutover checklist and a minimal rollback plan.

Looping in Ben to confirm procurement timeline.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan

Hi Tessa / team —

A few technical clarifications from infra/security before we lock the staging runbook:

1) SCIM delta behavior: when we push a change to employeeType in SCIM, will Redwood update roles in real time, or do we need a reconciliation job? We prefer near real-time.
2) Service accounts: we do not allow long-lived static API keys without HSM-backed rotation. If Redwood can accept short-lived OIDC tokens from our identity provider (IdP) for machine-to-machine, that’s preferred.
3) IP allowlist maintenance: will Redwood accept a signed JSON file (automated) with CIDR ranges that we push to the control plane (API)? Manual config is a no-go for us.
4) Test accounts: please confirm a safe set of test principals and the test data scope you need for the staging run.

Could someone share the scim-mapping.csv contents (if not sensitive) and a sample API call to update the allowlist? If you can provide the small runbook snippets in this thread I’ll forward to my ops team for review.

Thanks,

Daniel —

Thanks — answers inline and a brief staging runbook excerpt below.

1) SCIM delta behavior: Redwood supports near real-time SCIM provisioning using 200-based delta responses. Changes to employeeType are applied within ~30s in normal conditions. For safety we recommend a daily reconciliation job (example script attached in the playbook).

2) Service accounts: we support OIDC-based short-lived tokens for machine-to-machine auth. If you can issue tokens from your IdP we’ll accept them and map to a service principal. For HSM rotation we can integrate via your KMS (we have a connector for common providers).

3) IP allowlist API: yes — we provide a signed JSON payload endpoint (POST /v1/customers/{id}/allowlist) and validate signed timestamps. See sample below:

POST /v1/customers/EV-2028-0427/allowlist
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: {"cidrs": ["198.51.100.0/24", "203.0.113.0/24"], "signed_at": "2028-08-01T15:00:00Z", "signature": "..."}

(we will provide an SDK helper in the staging repo).

4) Test accounts: suggest two staging principals (svc-staging-ops and human-staging-admin) and a small dataset subset. We’ll provide test tokens and a separate staging tenancy so production data isn’t touched.

Staging runbook excerpt (for your ops):
- Step 0: Provision staging tenancy and confirm SCIM endpoint credentials.
- Step 1: Push SCIM mapping to staging and run a provisioning smoke test (10 users).
- Step 2: Add two CIDR ranges via allowlist API and confirm connectivity from staging agents.
- Step 3: Create service principal with OIDC token mapping and verify token exchange.
- Step 4: Execute a staged login/cutover window (1 hour) and validate audit logs export.

I’ll attach the sample scripts and the small reconciliation script to the drive link. Proposed time for the staging session: Aug 8 or Aug 9, 10am PT. Does that work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
